title: Adaptive audit-stream rate limiter + cost-aware partitioning & retention playbook
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Context: Audit traffic for RBAC changes, SSO/SAML events, and admin actions has grown 4x in the past 6 months and is causing spikes in ingestion costs and query latency for security dashboards. Goal: Implement an adaptive ingestion/throttling policy + cost-aware partitioning and retention playbook that preserves high-fidelity recent data for detection and compliance while bounding long-term storage cost. This ticket covers design, config knobs, rollout plan, and observability for the pipeline and storage side (indexing/partitioning/TTL/coldstore). Exclusions: log format/schema overhaul is tracked in ENG-69980, schema compatibility must be preserved.
acceptance_criteria: New adaptive rate limiter enforces per-tenant and global soft/hard limits with backpressure signals to producers
Partitioning scheme implemented that creates hourly hot partitions and daily cold partitions with automatic compaction
Retention policy: 90 days hot index (fast queries), 2 year coldstore with compacted indexes; cost does not exceed target budget by >10% in first 30 days
Telemetry: dashboards for ingestion rate, dropped/queued events, partition sizes, storage cost, and SLO violations
Rollout: canary to 5% tenants with rollback path and no data loss for events below hard limit
plan: Week 1: Design review with Infra/SEC/Platform; finalize partition key (tenant, event_type, day) and rate-limit algorithm (leaky-bucket with adaptive window)
Week 2: Implement ingest-side limiter + backpressure headers in gateway; add configurable tenant profiles (burst, steady)
Week 3: Storage: implement partitioner job, compaction pipeline to produce compacted daily blobs and purge raw hot shards older than 90d
Week 4: Observability: Grafana dashboard + alerts; synthetic load tests; cost projection run
Week 5: Canary rollout (5% tenants) -> monitor -> 25% -> 100% with nightly cost checks and rollback plan
risks: Over-aggressive throttling could drop events required for incident investigations
Partition compaction can be IO-heavy and interfere with real-time queries if not rate-limited
Integration with RBAC v2 audit producers may require minor client updates to handle backpressure headers
Coldstore retrieval latency may exceed compliance window for some ad-hoc queries
